issue_context.title: Netatmo: Entity x from integration netatmo has state class total_increasing, but its state is not strictly increasing
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Found this error in the HA log, using Netatmo with a public weather station:

```
Logger: homeassistant.components.sensor.recorder
Source: components/sensor/recorder.py:301
Integration: Sensor (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 5:00:10 PM (1 occurrences)
Last logged: 5:00:10 PM

Entity sensor.netatmo_loo_rain_today from integration netatmo has state class total_increasing, but its state is not strictly increasing. Triggered by state 4.1 (4.2) with last_updated set to 2024-02-26T15:55:44.469003+00:00. review_comments:
```
I don't think this is correct. Rain will not "unfall", thus `total` makes no sense here.

If this is a moving window, the state class should be removed.

../Frenck
I changed the rain sensors to MEASUREMENT, like all others, or do you want me to remove that completely for rain?

I guess that could work, but I wonder why this is happening in the first place?

I miss the motivation in this PR why the current value is wrong, and why the new choice is the right one?
See https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/111510, I see the value going down, maybe some water evaporates?

Well that is the question. Why is the value going down in this case. We need to know why that is, in order to make the right decision in this case.

It seems like this PR is fighting/aiming to resolve an error, but an explanation for the error being there is the first place, is missing?
Ok, I will make this draft and maybe  @cgtobi knows where to find the API docu from Netatmo explaining this
